title: Domain type and validation
text: The system shall define a Domain type (integer) validated to the range 0–232 inclusive, returning ErrDomainOutOfRange for values outside that range.

title: GUID type
text: The system shall define a Guid type as a 16-byte fixed-size array, matching the DDS writer GUID encoding in relay::Message meta key dds.writer_guid as a 32-character lowercase hex string.

title: QoS types and defaults
text: The system shall define ReliabilityKind (BestEffort=0, Reliable=1), DurabilityKind (Volatile=0, TransientLocal=1), and QoS struct with default_qos() and reliable_qos() factory functions.

title: Sample type and message conversion
text: The system shall define a Sample struct and implement lossless Sample::to_message() and from_message() per RELAY spec §15.7.2, including topic, payload, timestamp, seq, and writer_guid. The encoding must match the RELAY spec golden vector (topic=rt/chatter, seq=7, guid bytes 1–16, meta dds.writer_guid=0102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f10).

title: IPublisher interface
text: The system shall define an IPublisher abstract interface with write(payload), write(ctx, payload), and close() methods, returning ErrPayloadTooLarge when QoS.max_sample_size is exceeded and ErrTimeout when the context has expired.

title: ISubscriber interface
text: The system shall define an ISubscriber abstract interface with channel(), try_read(), unsubscribe(), and close() methods per RELAY spec §8.2.

title: IParticipant interface
text: The system shall define an IParticipant abstract interface with new_publisher(), new_subscriber(), domain(), and close() methods per RELAY spec §8.2.

title: DDS error sentinels
text: The system shall define a dds error category and the DDS-specific error codes ErrTopicEmpty, ErrQoSMismatch, ErrDeadlineMissed, ErrSampleRejected, ErrResourceLimits, ErrLoanBuffer, ErrDomainOutOfRange, each mapping to the closest relay sentinel per RELAY spec §5.3.

title: adapt() relay::INode bridge
text: The system shall provide adapt() to wrap an IParticipant as a relay::INode, forwarding send/subscribe/close and translating relay::Message ↔ dds::Sample per §15.7.2.

title: SampleFilter and with_filter subscriber option
text: The system shall provide a SampleFilter predicate type and a with_filter(pred) subscriber option that silently drops samples not matching the predicate before they reach the subscriber channel.

title: with_deadline_missed subscriber option
text: The system shall provide a with_deadline_missed(callback) subscriber option that invokes the callback when QoS.deadline elapses without a sample being received on the subscriber.

title: WaitSet — multiplex subscriber channels
text: The system shall provide a WaitSet class that multiplexes multiple subscriber channels onto a single wait_any() call, returning the first available sample and its source index. Equivalent to go-DDS WaitSet.

title: ILoaningPublisher — zero-copy loan-based write
text: The system shall provide an ILoaningPublisher interface extending IPublisher with loan_buffer(), write_loaned(), and return_loan() for zero-copy sample publishing equivalent to go-DDS LoaningPublisher (RELAY spec §8.3).

title: Mock participant factory
text: The system shall provide dds::mock::create(domain) returning an IMockParticipant that validates the domain and returns ErrDomainOutOfRange for out-of-range values.

title: Mock participant lifecycle
text: The mock participant's close() shall be idempotent; subsequent new_publisher() and new_subscriber() calls after close shall return ErrClosed.

title: Mock publish and in-process routing
text: Publishing a sample via IPublisher::write() shall deliver it to all matching subscribers in the same process via the global Broker, including monotonically increasing sequence numbers.

title: Mock subscriber channel and back-pressure
text: Each subscriber shall receive an independent channel with configurable depth and back-pressure policy (DropNewest, DropOldest, Block).

title: Mock unsubscribe semantics
text: After Unsubscribe() the channel is closed, further sends are silently dropped, and calling Unsubscribe() again is a no-op per RELAY spec §6.4.

title: Write metrics tracking
text: The mock participant shall track write_count and bytes_written incremented atomically on each successful IPublisher::write() call.

title: Delivery metrics tracking
text: The mock participant shall track deliver_count, drop_count, and bytes_delivered reflecting actual broker delivery outcomes per publish cycle.

title: IMetricsProvider interface
text: The mock participant shall implement relay::IMetricsProvider, exposing an atomic snapshot of all counters via metrics() with no side effects.

title: dds::IMetricsProvider interface
text: Both dds::mock and dds::rtps::Participant shall implement dds::IMetricsProvider — the DDS-package-scoped counterpart to relay::IMetricsProvider mirroring go-DDS's dds.MetricsProvider (dds.go) — exposing an atomic snapshot of write/deliver/drop counts and byte totals via dds_metrics() with no side effects.

title: dds::IDiscoveryMetricsProvider interface
text: Both dds::mock and dds::rtps::Participant shall implement dds::IDiscoveryMetricsProvider, mirroring go-DDS's dds.DiscoveryMetricsProvider (dds.go). The mock has no real network discovery and shall always return zero-valued DiscoveryMetrics; dds::rtps::Participant shall report live SPDP/SEDP counters (announces sent/received, known peers, peer evictions, endpoint matches).

title: dds::ITopicMetricsProvider interface
text: Both dds::mock and dds::rtps::Participant shall implement dds::ITopicMetricsProvider, mirroring go-DDS's dds.TopicMetricsProvider (dds.go), exposing topic_metrics() as a per-topic breakdown (write/deliver/drop counts and byte totals) of the aggregate dds::Metrics counters.

title: IHealthProvider — healthy status
text: The mock participant shall implement relay::IHealthProvider, returning HealthStatus::OK while active.

title: IHealthProvider — degraded on close
text: After close() the mock participant's health() shall return HealthStatus::Down.

title: dds::IHealthProvider interface
text: Both dds::mock and dds::rtps::Participant shall implement dds::IHealthProvider — the DDS-package-scoped counterpart to relay::IHealthProvider mirroring go-DDS's dds.HealthProvider (dds.go) — exposing a point-in-time participant/transport health snapshot via dds_health(), returning HealthStatus::Down with a JSON-encoded details string once closed and HealthStatus::OK otherwise. dds::rtps::Participant additionally folds live writer/reader counts into the details string when open, matching go-DDS's rtps.participant.Health() exactly.

title: Domain boundary enforcement
text: The system shall reject any domain identifier outside 0–232 inclusive before any object is created, preventing access to out-of-range DDS domains.

title: Payload size enforcement
text: When QoS.max_sample_size > 0 the system shall reject payloads exceeding that size with ErrPayloadTooLarge, preventing heap exhaustion from oversized samples.

title: Topic name validation
text: The system shall reject empty topic names with ErrTopicEmpty at the IParticipant level, preventing creation of publishers or subscribers on unnamed topics.

title: Write-after-close rejection
text: IPublisher::write() calls on a closed publisher or participant shall return ErrClosed without publishing any data.

title: Concurrent state access safety
text: All shared mutable state (Broker subscriptions, last-sample cache, participant counters) shall be protected by appropriate synchronisation primitives, ensuring data-race freedom under concurrent access.

title: Channel depth cap
text: The system shall define kMaxChanDepth = 4096 as the maximum allowed channel depth, preventing unbounded memory allocation from misconfigured subscribers.

title: IPublisher idempotent close
text: IPublisher::close() shall be idempotent: calling it multiple times shall not produce errors or undefined behaviour.

title: ISubscriber idempotent unsubscribe
text: ISubscriber::unsubscribe() shall be idempotent: calling it multiple times or after close() shall be a no-op.

title: IParticipant idempotent close
text: IParticipant::close() shall be idempotent: repeated calls shall return success without side effects.

title: Post-close participant operations
text: After IParticipant::close(), new_publisher() and new_subscriber() shall return ErrClosed with a null pointer.

title: Subscriber destructor auto-unsubscribes
text: The ISubscriber destructor shall automatically call unsubscribe(), ensuring the channel is closed and broker routing is cleaned up even if the caller does not explicitly unsubscribe.

title: Chan<T> bounded FIFO semantics
text: Chan<T> shall be a bounded FIFO channel with a configurable capacity; elements are delivered in the order inserted. The channel shall be non-copyable.

title: Chan<T> non-blocking try_send / try_recv
text: try_send() and try_recv() shall return immediately without blocking, returning Full/Closed or nullopt as appropriate.

title: Chan<T> closed-channel semantics
text: recv() on a closed and empty channel shall return nullopt immediately; send() on a closed channel shall return false immediately.

title: Chan<T> back-pressure policies
text: The Broker shall support three back-pressure policies: DropNewest (try_send, drop incoming when full), DropOldest (evict head, insert new), and Block (send, block sender until space available).

title: CLI: version subcommand
text: The cpp-dds CLI version subcommand shall print the RELAY spec version (1.7), the DDS protocol identifier (2), and the library semantic version.

title: CLI: conform subcommand
text: The cpp-dds CLI conform subcommand shall invoke the RELAY conform gate and exit with code 0 on success, non-zero on failure.

title: CLI: convert subcommand
text: The cpp-dds CLI convert --protocol P [--format json] subcommand shall read a dds.Sample JSON value on stdin, run it through Sample::to_message(), and write the resulting relay.Message JSON to stdout, per RELAY spec §11.2 (exit 0 converted / 1 invalid input / 2 invalid args).

title: Thread-safe shared state
text: All shared mutable state shall be protected by std::mutex, std::shared_mutex, or std::atomic; no data races shall be detectable under ASan/TSan analysis.

title: Error-code return discipline
text: All public API functions shall return std::error_code for failure signalling; no exceptions shall be thrown across public API boundaries.

title: Bounded execution time
text: All blocking API operations shall accept a relay::Context with timeout so callers can bound execution time and detect liveness failures.

title: Requirements traceability
text: Every source file shall carry fusa:req annotations linking implementation units to requirement identifiers; every test file shall carry fusa:test annotations linking test cases to the requirements they verify. The CI fusa-asil-b job shall validate that all requirements are both implemented and tested.

title: RELAY spec golden vector conformance
text: Sample::to_message() and from_message() must produce output that exactly matches the RELAY spec §15.7.2 golden vector: topic=rt/chatter, payload=[104,101,108,108,111,32,100,100,115], seq=7, writer_guid bytes [1..16], meta dds.writer_guid=0102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f10.

title: E2E protection wire header format
text: dds::safety shall define an 18-byte, little-endian E2E protection header — DataID (uint16, bytes 0-1), SourceID (uint16, bytes 2-3), SequenceCounter (uint32, bytes 4-7), Timestamp (int64 Unix nanoseconds, bytes 8-15), CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (uint16, bytes 16-17, computed with the CRC slot treated as zero) — byte-for-byte identical to go-DDS's safety/e2e.go, verified against independently derived reference vectors.

title: E2EPublisher prepends protection header
text: dds::safety::E2EPublisher shall wrap a dds::IPublisher and prepend the REQ-E2E-001 header to every payload before writing, with a per-publisher SequenceCounter that starts at 1 and increments monotonically on each write, thread-safe under concurrent write() calls (REQ-SAFETY-001).

title: E2ESubscriber CRC validation
text: dds::safety::E2ESubscriber shall strip the REQ-E2E-001 header from every received sample and validate its CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE checksum; on mismatch it shall report E2EErrorKind::CRCMismatch via errors() and MUST NOT forward the sample to channel().

title: E2ESubscriber sequence gap detection
text: dds::safety::E2ESubscriber shall detect gaps in the received SequenceCounter (any value other than the immediately preceding counter + 1) and report E2EErrorKind::SequenceGap via errors(); the sample MUST still be forwarded to channel() despite the gap.

title: E2ESubscriber freshness (staleness) check
text: When E2EConfig::max_age is non-zero, dds::safety::E2ESubscriber shall compute sample age as (now - header Timestamp) and report E2EErrorKind::StaleSample via errors() (without forwarding to channel()) when age exceeds max_age. When max_age is zero, freshness checking is disabled and samples of any age are forwarded.

title: E2ESubscriber short-payload rejection
text: dds::safety::E2ESubscriber shall report E2EErrorKind::HeaderTooShort via errors() (without forwarding to channel() or attempting CRC/sequence/freshness validation) whenever a received sample's payload is shorter than the 18-byte REQ-E2E-001 header.

title: Plugin interface contract
text: dds::security shall define a Plugin interface with seal() and open() operations that must be inverses of one another for any plaintext when both calls succeed; all built-in Plugin implementations shall be safe for concurrent use from multiple threads.

title: NullPlugin identity transform
text: dds::security::NullPlugin shall implement Plugin as the identity transform: seal() and open() return the input unchanged, providing neither confidentiality nor integrity.

title: HMACPlugin wire format
text: dds::security::HMACPlugin::seal() shall append a 32-byte HMAC-SHA-256 authentication tag computed over the plaintext to the end of the payload (wire format: plaintext || HMAC[32]), byte-for-byte identical to go-DDS's security.HMACPlugin, verified against reference vectors independently derived from a fresh go-DDS clone.

title: HMACPlugin tag verification
text: dds::security::HMACPlugin::open() shall recompute the HMAC-SHA-256 tag over the received plaintext and compare it in constant time against the trailing 32 bytes of the payload, returning ErrHMACTooShort for payloads shorter than 32 bytes and ErrHMACVerificationFailed when the tag does not match (including when opened with a different key than was used to seal).

title: AESGCMPlugin wire format
text: dds::security::AESGCMPlugin::seal() shall encrypt the plaintext with AES-256-GCM using a fresh random 12-byte nonce per call, producing wire format nonce[12] || ciphertext || GCM-tag[16], byte-for-byte identical to go-DDS's security.AESGCMPlugin, verified against reference vectors independently derived from a fresh go-DDS clone; new_aes_gcm_plugin() shall return ErrAESKeyInvalidLength when the supplied key is not exactly 32 bytes.

title: AESGCMPlugin authenticated decryption
text: dds::security::AESGCMPlugin::open() shall verify the GCM authentication tag and reject (ErrAESDecryptFailed) any payload that has been tampered with or was sealed under a different key, and shall return ErrAESPayloadTooShort for payloads shorter than the 12-byte nonce plus 16-byte tag; two seal() calls on identical plaintext shall never produce identical ciphertext (no nonce reuse).

title: Key material isolation and generation
text: HMACPlugin and AESGCMPlugin constructors shall copy caller-supplied key material so that subsequent mutation of the caller's buffer does not affect the plugin; new_random_key(n) shall return n cryptographically random bytes drawn from the OS entropy source, with each call producing distinct output.

title: Topic ACL rule evaluation
text: dds::security::AccessPolicy shall evaluate its Rule list in declaration order and grant access per the first Pattern that matches a given topic (glob semantics: '*' matches one path segment, not spanning '/'; '?' and '[...]' character classes as in Go's path.Match); a topic matching no rule, or an AccessPolicy with no rules, shall deny both Read and Write; a malformed pattern shall be skipped rather than causing an error or crash.

title: Anti-replay sequence enforcement
text: dds::security::ReplayGuard::check(seq, ts) shall record seq as seen at ts and return no error the first time a sequence number is presented within the configured sliding window, and shall return ErrReplay for any subsequent check() of the same sequence number within that window; entries older than the window (relative to the most recent check()/purge() call) shall be pruned; a non-positive window shall default to 30 seconds; ReplayGuard shall be safe for concurrent use from multiple threads.

title: XTypes type-descriptor model
text: dds::xtypes shall define TypeKind (Bool, Int32, Int64, Float64, String, Bytes, Struct, Seq), FieldDescriptor (name, kind, optional, nested fields for Struct, element descriptor for Seq), and TypeDescriptor (name, version, top-level fields), field-for-field mirrors of go-DDS's xtypes.TypeKind/FieldDescriptor/TypeDescriptor.

title: Content-addressed TypeIdentifier
text: dds::xtypes::identify(td) shall compute a TypeIdentifier whose hash is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over a canonical JSON encoding of td, byte-for-byte identical to go-DDS's xtypes.Identify()/canonical() output (compact encoding, map keys sorted lexicographically, Go's default HTML-safe string escaping), verified against reference vectors independently derived from a fresh go-DDS clone; two descriptors that differ only in field declaration order shall produce identical TypeIdentifiers, and any difference in name, field name, kind, optional flag, nested field, or sequence element shall produce a different hash.

title: DynamicData schema-validated field access
text: dds::xtypes::DynamicData::set(name, value) shall return ErrUnknownField when name is not declared among the backing TypeDescriptor's top-level fields, and shall otherwise store value; DynamicData::get(name) shall return an empty result for a declared-but-unset field, distinct from a field that has never been declared at all.

title: DynamicData JSON serialization and forward compatibility
text: DynamicData::to_json() shall serialise all set fields to a compact JSON object; DynamicData::from_json(text) shall fully parse and syntactically validate the entire input document before applying any field (a malformed value anywhere fails the whole call, even under an unknown key), shall silently skip (not store) any key not declared in the backing TypeDescriptor (forward compatibility), shall decode JSON numbers as double-precision values regardless of their textual shape (matching Go's json.Unmarshal-into-`any` behavior of always producing float64), and shall return ErrInvalidJSON for malformed input or a non-object top-level value.

title: TypeObject construction
text: dds::xtypes::new_type_object(td) shall return a TypeObject pairing td with identify(td), computing the identifier automatically.

title: Type-evolution compatibility checking
text: dds::xtypes::check_compatibility(writer_td, reader_td) shall report compatible=true when every reader field either exists in the writer with the same TypeKind or is absent from the writer but marked Optional in the reader; it shall report compatible=false (with a human-readable reason) when a required reader field is absent from the writer or when a shared field's TypeKind differs between writer and reader; fields present in the writer but absent from the reader shall never cause incompatibility.

title: TypeRegistry store and lookup
text: dds::xtypes::TypeRegistry::register_type(to) shall store to keyed by to->id.name; TypeRegistry::lookup(name) shall return the stored TypeObject for a registered name or nullptr for an unregistered one.

title: TypeRegistry name-conflict detection
text: TypeRegistry::register_type(to) shall return ErrTypeMismatch when a TypeObject with the same name but a different content-addressed hash is already registered, and shall be a no-op (success) when the same TypeObject (same name and hash) is registered again.

title: TypeRegistry snapshot and thread safety
text: TypeRegistry::all() shall return a snapshot of every registered TypeObject sorted by name; TypeRegistry shall be safe for concurrent register_type()/lookup()/all() calls from multiple threads.

title: CDR_LE encapsulation header
text: dds::cdr::Encoder shall prepend the 4-byte CDR_LE encapsulation header ({0x01,0x00,0x00,0x00}) to every buffer it produces; dds::cdr::Decoder::create() shall validate and consume that header, returning std::nullopt when the buffer is shorter than 4 bytes or the 2-byte little-endian scheme field is neither 0x0001 (CDR_LE) nor 0x0000 (CDR_BE); a decoder created from an accepted CDR_BE-scheme header shall still decode the remaining payload little-endian.

title: CDR encoder alignment
text: dds::cdr::Encoder shall pad bytes between fields to enforce natural alignment: 2-byte for int16/uint16, 4-byte for int32/uint32/float32, 8-byte for int64/uint64/float64; bool/int8/uint8 fields shall not be padded. The encapsulation header shall count toward alignment.

title: CDR decoder alignment and underrun detection
text: dds::cdr::Decoder shall enforce the same alignment rules as dds::cdr::Encoder, advancing past padding bytes before every aligned read, and every read_*() method shall return std::nullopt (never read out of bounds or invoke undefined behavior) when fewer bytes remain in the buffer than the field requires, including when a string or byte-sequence's declared length exceeds the remaining buffer.

title: CDR string and bytes encoding
text: dds::cdr::Encoder::write_string(s) shall encode a 4-byte-aligned uint32 length (s.size()+1, for the null terminator) followed by s's raw bytes and a trailing null byte; an empty string shall encode as length=1 followed by a single null byte. dds::cdr::Encoder::write_bytes(b) shall encode a 4-byte-aligned uint32 count (b.size()) followed by b's raw bytes with no null terminator. dds::cdr::Decoder::read_string() shall strip the trailing null terminator from its result; read_bytes() shall not.

title: CDR encoder/decoder length introspection
text: dds::cdr::Encoder::len() shall return the current total encoded length including the 4-byte encapsulation header; dds::cdr::Decoder::remaining() shall return the number of bytes not yet consumed from the buffer, both updating incrementally as fields are written or read.

title: Module/struct/enum/typedef parsing
text: dds::idl::parse_string() shall parse module declarations (which may be nested), struct declarations with ordered fields, enum declarations with ordered enumerator names, and typedef alias declarations, returning a Module tree that mirrors the source's declaration order and nesting.

title: Basic IDL type parsing
text: dds::idl::parse_string() shall recognize the basic IDL types boolean, octet, short, unsigned short, long, unsigned long, long long, unsigned long long, float, double, and string (bounded or unbounded, string<N>'s bound N being parsed and discarded), mapping each to the corresponding dds::idl::TypeKind.

title: Sequence, array, and qualified-name parsing
text: dds::idl::parse_string() shall parse bounded and unbounded sequence<T>[, N] (the bound N being parsed and discarded), fixed-size arrays T name[N] (recording the element count), and qualified type references Module::Name (recording the full dotted-path RefName, deferring struct-vs-enum resolution to code generation).

title: @key annotation parsing
text: dds::idl::parse_string() shall set Field::key = true for a struct field preceded by an @key annotation and false otherwise; other bare (argument-less) annotations shall be recognized and skipped without affecting the parsed field. A parenthesized annotation argument (e.g. @id(5)) is not supported and shall produce a parse error, matching go-DDS's own parser behavior exactly (verified against a fresh go-DDS clone) rather than silently accepting or fixing it.

title: Parse error reporting and malformed-input safety
text: dds::idl::parse_string()/parse_file() shall return a ParseResult with no Module and a populated ParseError (carrying a 1-based source line number and a human-readable message) for malformed input, including an unexpected token, a missing '{'/'}'/';, an invalid or missing array size, an unknown type after 'unsigned', or an unterminated sequence/struct/enum; malformed input shall never crash, hang, or invoke undefined behavior.

title: C++ struct/enum/typedef code generation
text: dds::idl::generate() shall emit, for every struct/enum/typedef in the Module tree (including nested sub-modules, flattened into one namespace), a corresponding C++ struct (fields in declaration order, field/type names verbatim from the IDL source), enum class backed by int32_t (enumerators in declaration order starting at 0), or type alias (using Name = UnderlyingType;), inside a namespace derived from the root Module's name (lowercased) or "idlgen" if the root Module's name is empty.

title: CDR codec code generation
text: dds::idl::generate() shall emit, for every IDL struct, a <Name>Codec type with a static marshal() building a dds::cdr::Encoder-backed byte buffer and a static unmarshal() building a dds::cdr::Decoder-backed std::optional<Name>, correctly handling primitive fields, strings, octet sequences (write_bytes/read_bytes), general sequences (uint32 length prefix plus per-element encode/decode), fixed arrays (no length prefix), and nested struct/enum/typedef references recursively inlined at the call site with no wrapper header (matching CDR wire semantics) and guarded against infinite recursion on a self-referential struct graph.

title: Key-field introspection code generation
text: The generated <Name>Codec::key_fields() shall return, in declaration order, the names of every field marked @key in the source IDL struct, or an empty vector when no field is marked @key.

title: ddstool idl subcommand CLI behavior
text: The ddstool executable's idl subcommand shall parse an input .idl file via dds::idl::parse_file(), generate C++ source via dds::idl::generate(), and write it to stdout by default or to the file named by -out when given; an optional -namespace flag shall override the root Module's name before generation. ddstool help/-h/--help shall print usage information and exit 0; an unknown subcommand, a missing required <input.idl> argument, or a parse/generate failure shall print a descriptive message to stderr and exit with a non-zero status.

title: TSN stream descriptor and StreamConfig JSON loading
text: The system shall define dds::tsn::Stream (topic, vid, pcp, dscp, max_frame_size, max_interval_frames, interval_us, tx_offset_us, talker_id) and dds::tsn::StreamConfig (a vector of Stream plus stream_for_topic()/topics()/to_json()), and load_config()/parse_config() functions that parse a JSON tsn_streams document into a StreamConfig, validating topic non-empty, PCP in 0–7, DSCP in 0–63, and max_frame_size/max_interval_frames/interval_us/tx_offset_us all ≥ 0, returning a diagnostic on any violation or malformed JSON.

title: TSNStreamConfig resolution and Participant wiring
text: The system shall define dds::rtps::TSNParams and the dds::rtps::TSNStreamConfig interface (stream_for_topic(topic, out)), dds::tsn::StreamConfigAdapter/with_stream_config() adapting a StreamConfig to that interface, and ParticipantOptions::tsn_config: when set, dds::rtps::Participant::new_publisher shall resolve each new writer's topic against it and, on a match, route that writer's remote DATA and HEARTBEAT sends through a dedicated UDP socket with SO_PRIORITY set to the stream's PCP and IP_TOS set to the stream's DSCP<<2, reusing one socket per distinct PCP value across writers.

title: QoS::transport_priority fallback PCP selection
text: When a writer's topic has no matching TSN stream configured, dds::rtps::Participant::new_publisher shall, if QoS::transport_priority is greater than 0, use it (clamped to 7) as a fallback SO_PRIORITY value on a dedicated per-PCP socket with no DSCP marking and no scheduled transmit, matching the resolution otherwise falling back to the participant's shared data socket. QoS::latency_budget shall remain purely informational (read by no send-path logic), matching go-DDS.
standards: go-DDS rtps/participant.go NewPublisher "Wire TSN stream" fallback branch

title: SO_TXTIME-scheduled transmit for TSN streams with a nonzero tx_offset
text: For a writer resolved against a TSN stream whose tx_offset is nonzero, Writer::write() shall compute a scheduled transmit time (nanoseconds since the CLOCK_TAI epoch) as the next stream-interval boundary plus tx_offset, and send each remote DATA/DATA_FRAG message via dds::rtps::scheduled_send on the writer's dedicated TSN socket, falling back to an immediate send when CLOCK_TAI is unavailable, the socket has no dedicated TSN socket, or the stream's interval is zero.

title: TSN stream MaxFragPayload bounds writer fragmentation
text: Stream::max_frag_payload() shall return max_frame_size minus 48 (or 0 when max_frame_size is unset or ≤ 48). A writer resolved against a TSN stream with a nonzero max_frag_payload shall use it, instead of fragment.hpp's default kMaxFragmentPayload, as the DATA/DATA_FRAG fragmentation threshold for every write.

title: TAPRIOConfig gate control list, validation, and derivation
text: The system shall define dds::tsn::TAPRIOEntry (gate_mask, interval) and TAPRIOConfig (cycle_time, entries, interface, base_time, offload) with cycle_duration() (explicit cycle_time or the sum of entry intervals), validate() (non-empty interface, non-empty entries, every entry interval > 0 and ≤ the kernel's uint32 nanosecond limit), tc_command() (a portable tc(8) command-string template), and taprio_from_streams() (deriving a TAPRIOConfig from a StreamConfig, one gate entry per stream keyed by PCP as the traffic class), all available and platform-independent on every target.

title: TAPRIOConfig::apply/verify_applied — Linux netlink, portable stub elsewhere
text: On Linux, TAPRIOConfig::apply() shall program the kernel taprio qdisc on Interface via an RTM_NEWQDISC request over NETLINK_ROUTE (replacing any existing root qdisc) and TAPRIOConfig::verify_applied() shall confirm it via RTM_GETQDISC, both requiring CAP_NET_ADMIN; on every other platform, both shall return a "TAPRIO qdisc requires Linux" diagnostic without attempting any OS call. The platform split shall be a CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME-gated translation-unit split (taprio_linux.cpp / taprio_other.cpp), matching this repo's traffic_linux.cpp/traffic_other.cpp precedent.
